titel: An investment policy statement in five lines
kurz: Allocation, building blocks, contributions, rebalancing and emergencies are the five decisions that fully describe an investment policy, and none of them can be left out.

bloecke.md:
A portfolio is first and foremost a set of rules and only secondarily a collection of products. The products can be exchanged without anything essential changing, but the rules cannot. What a private investor has to decide fits on one page and consists of five lines:

1. The **allocation** states how much of your wealth carries equity risk.
2. For the **equity portion**, you determine which building blocks it consists of.
3. The **contributions** specify which amount flows into which building block and when.
4. The **rebalancing rule** describes when and by what means the allocation is restored.
5. The **emergency rule** specifies what happens in the event of a crash, a loss of income and a tax debit, and what explicitly does not happen.

These five decisions have to be made anyway. Investors who do not write them down beforehand make them later under pressure, with prices falling and without a benchmark.
The allocation determines the risk; the choice of products changes the result only slightly. Anyone who starts by searching for ETFs when opening a securities account skips the most important line.

## Line 1 (allocation)

The risky part and the low-risk part have two separate tasks. The first is meant to generate returns and may fluctuate in order to do so; the second is meant not to fluctuate and may earn little in return. If long maturities or weaker credit ratings are added to make the low-risk part more profitable, a second equity risk enters the portfolio.

The level of the allocation results from two variables. The first is the point in time when the money will be needed. Money earmarked for the next five years does not belong in the equity portion. The second is the book loss you can tolerate without acting. It is measured in euros and not as a percentage. With wealth of €200,000 and an equity allocation of 60%, a decline like the one between October 2007 and March 2009 means that €120,000 becomes around €51,000. The decline drags on for sixteen months, and during that time nobody knows when the low point will be reached.

bloecke.titel: Maximum decline of the major world indices
bloecke.unter: Decline from peak to trough, gross in US dollars, for World and ACWI from 31 Oct 2007 to 9 Mar 2009. There is less than one percentage point between the narrowest and the broadest world index.

bloecke.md:
Diversification therefore decides which market determines the result. How far the portfolio falls in a crash is controlled by the allocation alone.

## Line 2 (equity portion)

There are several common designs for the equity portion. They differ less in expected return than in the effort needed to maintain them. Between one and four building blocks, what mainly changes is the number of allocations you have to maintain permanently, while diversification changes little. Every additional allocation produces a deviation every year, and in Germany every correction through a sale is a taxable event.

bloecke.titel: Designs for the equity portion (example products, as of July to September 2026)
zeilen: FTSE All-World or MSCI ACWI IMI
From 0.12% in the world building block
World + emerging markets + small caps + region or factor
Kommer ETF, weighted half by market capitalisation and half by GDP

bloecke.md: The US share varies particularly widely. The name *MSCI World* suggests the whole world, but the index contains only 23 developed markets, without emerging markets and without small companies. justETF reported a US share of 70.32% for the iShares Core MSCI World as of 31 August 2026, while the MSCI factsheet as of the same date gave 72.14%. The discrepancy is due to the different data bases and country classifications of the two sources. The high share follows from weighting by market capitalisation and is not a flaw of the product. However, choosing an index also means deciding on the US share, consciously or unconsciously.

bloecke.unter: All the building blocks shown are offered as global equity investments; depending on the index rule, their US share is between 45% and 70%. Values according to justETF, as of the end of August 2026.

bloecke.md:
Which variant is chosen is of secondary importance, as long as it matches your own willingness to look after the portfolio. However, the choice is recorded in line 2 and not decided anew every two years. Every change of building block is a sale followed by a purchase, and [[Flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer)|flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer)]] is due on the gain accrued up to that point.

## Line 3 (contributions)

Line 3 specifies which amount flows into which building block on which day. This means a savings plan that has actually been set up, not a mere intention. With only one building block, this line is simple. With two building blocks in a ratio of 70 to 30, €400 becomes two executions of €280 and €120. Special payments such as a bonus or an inheritance are split according to the same target allocation and not according to mood.

The execution fee is important for this line, because it has an effect even on small amounts, where the [[Tracking difference|tracking difference]] is still negligible. Outside its changing list of promotional offers, ING most recently charged 1.75% of the monthly contribution (as of September 2026). With a contribution of €300, that is €5.25 per execution and €63 a year. An ETF with an expense ratio of 0.14% only costs the same amount at a portfolio value of €45,000. At large neobrokers such as Scalable Capital, savings plan executions were free of charge on the same date. Inducements paid by the trading venue to the broker, which used to fund such executions, have also been banned in Germany since 1 July 2026 (Article 39a MiFIR). Costs are still incurred, because the spread between the bid and ask price is included in the execution price and does not appear on the contract note. Percentage fees burden each contribution with the same proportion. Fixed fees per execution, on the other hand, make splitting across several ETFs more expensive. With a monthly contribution of €75, this is the strongest reason to pay into only one ETF.

## Line 4 (rebalancing rule)

[[Rebalancing]] is covered separately in this course. The investment policy only contains the trigger, the date and the means. A band rather than a pure calendar has proven effective. The allocation is checked once a year, but action is only taken if it deviates by more than five percentage points in absolute terms or by a quarter in relative terms. In Germany, the means is almost always redirecting new contributions rather than selling.

The target portfolio is designed for 70/30, and the total value is €50,000. After a strong year for equities, €39,000 is in the equity portion and €11,000 in the low-risk part. This corresponds to 78 to 22, so the band of five percentage points has been exceeded.

With route A, €4,000 of equities are sold. If 40% of this amount is gain, that is a gain of €1,600. After the 30% [[Partial exemption (Teilfreistellung)|partial exemption (Teilfreistellung)]], €1,120 of it is taxable, which at 26.375% results in around €295 in tax. The allocation is then immediately back on target.

With route B, the next contributions flow entirely into the low-risk part. For €39,000 to make up 70% again, the portfolio has to grow to €55,700. This requires around €5,700 of new money. At €400 a month, this takes just over fourteen months. No tax is incurred.

Route B needs more money and more time. Route A costs €295, which then no longer earns any return. As long as the monthly contributions continue, route B is cheaper. If no more contributions are coming in or the deviation lies far outside the band, route A is the better choice.

## Line 5 (emergency rule)

The last line describes three events that are certain to occur and sets out the response to each of them. This is the only line in which the word *not* may appear.

bloecke.titel: Three triggers and the responses decided in advance
bloecke.unter: For each row, the response has been decided in advance, so that when an event occurs, the only thing left to check is which case applies.

bloecke.md: The third case is the one most often overlooked, because it has nothing to do with the stock exchange. The [[Advance lump sum (Vorabpauschale)|advance lump sum (Vorabpauschale)]] is only deemed to have been received on the first working day of the following year (Section 18(3) InvStG, Investment Tax Act). The bank then automatically collects the tax on it from the settlement account. If the account does not hold enough money, banks draw on linked accounts, ask the customer to pay money in or report the matter to the tax office (Section 44(1) EStG, Income Tax Act). For 2026, the Bundesbank determined a base interest rate (Basiszins) of 3.20% from the yield curve on the first trading day of the year (BMF circular of 13 January 2026). The base return (Basisertrag) is 70% of this, that is, 2.24% of the fund value at the start of the year.

The portfolio holds an accumulating equity ETF worth €120,000 on 2 January 2026. Over the course of the year, the price rises by at least 2.24%, and therefore by at least the base return, so the cap at the year's increase in value does not apply.

- Base return: 120,000 x 3.20% x 0.7 = €2,688 (Section 18(1) InvStG)
- Less distributions: none, because the fund accumulates
- Taxable after 30% partial exemption: €1,881.60 (Section 20(1) InvStG)
- Less [[Saver's allowance (Sparerpauschbetrag)|saver's allowance (Sparerpauschbetrag)]] of €1,000: €881.60 (Section 20(9) EStG)
- Tax at 26.375%: €232.52

The bank collects this amount on the first banking day in January 2027, even though no income has been paid out. It is not lost, because on a later sale all the advance lump sums recognised reduce the capital gain in full (Section 19(1) InvStG).

bloecke.titel: Selling because of a tax debit
bloecke.md: If there is not enough money in the settlement account in January and fund units are sold as a result, a mere prepayment turns into a genuine taxable event. The sale realises gains and ends the tax deferral on these units. A calendar entry in December reminding you to make sure the account is funded avoids this and costs nothing.

bloecke.titel: The five lines in an example (not a recommendation)
zeilen: 70% equities, 30% instant-access savings and money market
Horizon over 20 years; a decline like 2008 equals approx. 40% of the total portfolio
One accumulating world ETF, domiciled in Ireland, fund size over €1bn
No second building block that would need maintaining
€400 on the first of each month, entirely into the world ETF; special payments by target allocation
Fee-free execution, no recurring decision on how to split
Review on 15 January; adjustment via new contributions; sale only if the equity allocation is still above 75% after six months
A sale costs 26.375% on 70% of the gain
Savings plan continues; if income is lost, pause instead of selling; from December, €300 in the settlement account as cover
The emergency fund covers the loss of income; the tax on the advance lump sum is collected automatically

bloecke.md: The document covers one page with the date and your own signature and has a fixed annual review date. Two additional rules ensure that it remains binding. Changes are justified and dated, and they take effect no earlier than thirty days after they are entered. This waiting period is the most important safeguard, because it separates a change of mind from a panic reaction.

Price targets, economic forecasts, entry points and conditions of the form “when the market gets too expensive” do not belong in the five lines. Such sentences look like rules but are forecasts. With them, the document becomes a licence to intervene. You can recognise a rule by the fact that a third party could carry it out without an opinion of their own.

bloecke.titel: An investment policy for two people
bloecke.md:
The saver's allowance is €1,000 per person per year, or €2,000 jointly for spouses who are assessed jointly (Section 20(9) EStG). When the bank deducts tax, it only takes effect through exemption orders (Freistellungsaufträge) that have been submitted. Investors with securities accounts at several banks have to split the amount. Otherwise one bank collects tax while part of the allowance remains unused at the other. The tax overpaid is then only refunded via the tax return (Section 32d(4) EStG).

For two people, one joint document with two signatures is sufficient. Separate securities accounts make it easier to assign assets if your circumstances change. A joint securities account is more convenient day to day, but in the event of a separation or inheritance it can only be disentangled with more effort. None of this changes the five lines themselves.

mitnehmen: The five lines on allocation, building blocks, contributions, rebalancing and emergencies describe a portfolio completely; everything else is secondary.
Risk is controlled through the allocation and not through the choice of index; in the financial crisis, the MSCI World and MSCI ACWI lost 57.5% and 58.1% respectively.

Every additional building block brings a little more diversification but makes the portfolio permanently more demanding to maintain and causes more occasions for rebalancing and more flat-rate withholding tax.
The allocation is adjusted first through new contributions, because a sale costs 26.375% tax on 70% of the gain and this amount then no longer earns any return.
The emergency rule is set before the emergency, including funds to cover the tax on the advance lump sum, which is debited in January without any incoming payment.

begriffe.text: Written set of rules for a portfolio covering the target allocation, building blocks, contributions, rebalancing rule and emergency rule. It is drawn up in calm times so that it applies in turbulent ones.
Fixed share of the risky part in total wealth. The target allocation determines how much the portfolio loses in euros in a market decline.

Tolerance range around the target allocation, for example five percentage points in absolute terms or a quarter in relative terms. Action is only taken when the allocation leaves this range. This significantly reduces the number of transactions.
Response defined in advance to a crash, a loss of income and an automatic tax debit. It also covers the cases in which explicitly nothing happens.
